findings.title: AssignmentSource queued default is evaluated at import time
findings.body: The dataclass uses `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` as a default. Dataclass defaults are evaluated once when the class is defined, so every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` value, including via `from_integration`, gets the module import timestamp rather than the time the assignment source was actually created. Any logic that later reads `queued` for ordering, expiry, or burst detection will see all sources with the same stale timestamp. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: New should_sync argument can break subclass overrides
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` with a second positional argument. The base classes were updated to accept this argument, but `should_sync` is a polymorphic method that integrations commonly override with the previous one-argument signature to customize per-direction sync behavior. Any such override now raises `TypeError` on this line, causing assignee-sync tasks to crash instead of running. The same contract concern applies to the new `assignment_source` kwarg passed to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound` for overrides that do not accept `**kwargs`. All existing subclasses/overrides need to be audited and updated, or the call must be made backward-compatible.

findings.title: Missing test for propagation to a different integration
findings.body: The new suppression test only covers an assignment source whose integration matches the outbound target and asserts that outbound sync is not called. There is no test for the other required branch: when an inbound assignment comes from integration A and the group also has a linked issue for integration B, the outbound sync to B should still be scheduled. The same gap exists for inbound deassignment with a matching source. Without this coverage, an over-broad suppression would not be caught.
